title: Given a binary tree with an extra `next` pointer on each node, connect all nodes so that `next` forms a single continuous chain in level order: the last node of each level points to the first node of the next level, not to null.
shortTitle: Connect All Level Order Siblings (One Continuous Next Chain)

s1_definition.oneliner: BFS without level breaks: link every dequeued node's `next` to the very next dequeued node across all levels, forming one continuous chain.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **No level boundaries** – the `next` chain spans the entire tree in BFS order.
- **Single previous pointer** – one `previous` pointer persists for the whole traversal, never reset.
- **Continuous chain** – the last node of level k points to the first node of level k+1.
- **Termination** – only the very last node of the tree has `next = null`.
- **Complexity** – O(n) time, O(w) space for the queue.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India wants one continuous escalation path through every approver in breadth-first order. A request flows from the last approver on a rank straight to the first approver on the next rank without stopping. You clip every approver to the next one in the whole BFS sweep.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Before:                     After (continuous chain):
       1                       1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 7 -> null
      / \                      |
     2   3                  ┌──┴──────────────────────────────┐
    / \    \                │  Level boundaries are crossed:  │
   4   5    7               │  3 -> 4 (level 1 end to        │
                            │        level 2 start)           │
                            └─────────────────────────────────┘

  Connect-Siblings vs Connect-All:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Siblings:                                │
  │   1 -> null                              │
  │   2 -> 3 -> null                         │
  │   4 -> 5 -> 7 -> null                    │
  │                                          │
  │ Connect-All:                             │
  │   1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 7 -> null    │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Code Difference:
  Siblings:   TreeNode prev = null; (inside while, resets)
  Connect-All: TreeNode prev = null; (outside while, persists)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Connect All Level Order Siblings produces one continuous next chain threading every node in BFS order, crossing level boundaries instead of terminating each level with null. The solution is the same BFS loop as connect-siblings, but with one crucial difference: the previous pointer persists for the entire traversal and never resets at level boundaries.

Because there are no level breaks, the level-size snapshot is not needed, making the code simpler. You dequeue one node at a time, link the previous node's next to it, and advance previous. Only the very last node of the tree keeps next as null.

At the National Bank of India, this built a continuous escalation thread through every approver in BFS order. An automated sweep could walk from the branch head through every approver without reasoning about level boundaries, simplifying sequential processing.

The senior insight is being able to state the precise difference from connect-siblings in one sentence: previous resets per level for siblings, persists globally for connect-all. Both are identical BFS traversals; the single boolean decision of where to declare previous determines which variant you get.

Remember one sentence: Connect-all is BFS with a single persistent previous pointer that never resets, creating one continuous next chain across all levels.

---

keyPoints: One persistent previous pointer across the entire traversal; never reset at level boundaries.
The last node of each level points to the first node of the next level.
Level-size snapshot is not needed since there are no level breaks.
Only the very last node of the tree has next = null.
Time O(n), space O(w) for the queue.
The only difference from connect-siblings is where previous is declared and whether it resets.
